title: Sonu Nigam Apologises to Kannadigas Ahead of Bengaluru Concert on October 24
excerpt: In a video message, the singer said he does not mind saying sorry a thousand times over his April 2025 Pahalgam remark; Karnataka Rakshana Vedike has called off its protest against the concert.
body:
• Sonu Nigam has apologised to Kannadigas in a video message over his April 2025 remarks linking a Kannada song request to the Pahalgam terror attack, ahead of his Bengaluru concert on October 24.
  • The apology followed a demand by Karnataka Rakshana Vedike (KRV) that Bengaluru police deny permission for the concert, and a conversation between the singer and KRV president TA Narayana Gowda.
  • KRV has called off its planned protest against the concert after Gowda shared the singer's video message on October 19.
  • Nigam said Karnataka audiences have given him love and respect for 30 years and that he did not want a misunderstanding to damage that relationship.

Apology in a video message ahead of the concert

Singer Sonu Nigam has apologised to Kannadigas over remarks he made at a Bengaluru concert in April 2025, days before he is scheduled to perform in the city again on October 24. In a video message, Nigam addressed Karnataka audiences as his family and said he was willing to apologise repeatedly if that preserved the relationship. He spoke the opening lines in Kannada, according to Bollywood Hungama.

https://x.com/ndtv/status/2112472438542119264

"When you love someone and want the relationship to last, you don't mind saying sorry a thousand times."

— Sonu Nigam, Singer

"So, my dear family, if anything I've said inadvertently has hurt you, I'm so sorry. You know I'm not the kind of person who would ever hurt anyone, especially my family from Karnataka. You have given me so much love and respect over the last 30 years, and I don't want any small misunderstanding to taint that relationship or cause any bitterness," he added in the message.

The remark that started the controversy

The controversy dates to April 2025, when Nigam performed at East Point College of Engineering and Technology in Bengaluru. A member of the audience repeatedly demanded that he sing in Kannada. Nigam objected to the manner of the demand and, as quoted by NDTV, said: "The best songs I have sung are in Kannada... I didn't like it when a boy asked me to sing in Kannada. He was so rudely threatening, 'Kannada, Kannada.' This is the reason for the Pahalgam attack." The Pahalgam attack took place on April 22, 2025, when gunmen killed 26 tourists at Baisaran meadow near Pahalgam in Jammu and Kashmir. The comparison drew criticism from sections of the Kannada-speaking community, and the issue stayed alive in the months that followed.

KRV's demand, and its withdrawal

The dispute resurfaced this month when the pro-Kannada organisation Karnataka Rakshana Vedike demanded that the Bengaluru City Police Commissioner deny permission for Nigam's October 24 concert and warned of protests if it went ahead. Nigam then held what he described as a warm and respectful discussion with KRV state president TA Narayana Gowda. Gowda shared the singer's video message on October 19 and said Nigam had acknowledged that his remarks had hurt Kannadigas. Following the apology, the organisation decided to call off its planned protest against the concert, according to The Times of Bengal.

What's next

The Bengaluru concert is scheduled for October 24, with the protest called off and permission no longer contested by KRV. Nigam, one of India's most recorded playback singers across Hindi, Kannada and several other languages, has said he wants to put the episode behind him — and the October 24 performance will be the first test of whether the audience response matches the reconciliation.
